A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same foundation-model-assisted semi-supervised learning work. The complete main texts, figures, equations, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across eight datasets, coarse-label experiments, training-accuracy curves, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and zero-shot evaluations, component ablations, embedding experiments, sensitivity results, and measured computational costs. These extend beyond the externally attributed comparison scores.

M1.justification: v1's one-stage auxiliary-head ZMT becomes the second stage of ZeroMatch, preceded by new teacher-pseudolabel distillation into the main classifier (Section 4). v2 also adds embedding concatenation into both classifier heads (Appendix B.4). ZMT+ is no longer separately specified and evaluated, although its strong-augmentation memory-saving idea survives in Appendix D.4.

E1.justification: Flowers102 and Resisc45 add flower recognition and remote-sensing coverage. Yelp Review and all three audio datasets—UrbanSound8K, ESC-50, and GTZAN—are removed, while CIFAR100, Yahoo Answers, AG News, and Amazon Review remain. The Amazon experiment using three-class pseudolabels for five-class prediction is also removed.

E2.justification: v2 adds the evaluated PL feature input baseline and comparisons with published FineSSL, GRIP, and CPL results (Appendix C.1). Supervised, ReMixMatch, FlexMatch, and SimMatch rows disappear from retained benchmark comparisons. Doubly robust self-training remains for Yahoo Answers and Amazon Review in Table 13, but its CIFAR100 and AG News comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds a full distillation-stage training budget, introduces GPT and Llama teachers, revises FLAN-T5 teacher selection, and replaces best-of-four hyperparameter selection with fixed alpha_p=1 and lambda_p=1. Reporting switches from error to accuracy. Tables also change AG News's largest labeled set from 100 to 200 and Amazon's test count from 65,000 to 650,000; these reported revisions do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons removing auxiliary distillation or stage 1 (Tables 15-16), tests embedding augmentation (Table 5), and measures computational costs (Table 18). It removes v1's coarse-label study and unlabeled-prediction learning curves (Figures 2-3). The broader sensitivity sweeps are replaced by a smaller Yahoo Answers/Amazon Review analysis in Table 17.

E5.justification: Both versions retain medians and standard deviations over three seeds. v2 adds explicit ±0.00 reporting to zero-shot rows, while omitting v1's explanation connecting randomization to model initialization and labeled-sample selection. No increased run count or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: v2 reports substantial new two-stage, teacher, benchmark, ablation, and resource results, including 88.01±0.05% accuracy for CIFAR100 with 100 labels and GPT-4.1 pseudolabels (Table 3). Yelp, audio, and coarse-label results disappear. Some original one-stage scores survive as the without-stage-1 rows in Table 16; retained baselines converted from error to accuracy are not new performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds the first-stage distillation objective and changes the stated unsupervised-loss input from p(y|x_i) to p(y|u_i). The original auxiliary-head objective is otherwise retained under new notation. Dataset definitions, the foundation-model training-overlap assumption, and doubly robust formulas remain; neither version supplies new theoretical guarantees or proofs for the proposed method.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from multitask pseudolabel integration explicitly avoiding distillation to a framework explicitly combining distillation and SSL. The abstract and introduction replace the eight-dataset, three-domain and up-to-56%-error-reduction claims with six vision/language benchmarks and compact-student training through inference-only foundation-model access. Robustness to pseudolabel quality remains a central claim.

C2.justification: v2 introduces warm-start and catastrophic-forgetting explanations for the two stages, embedding-complementarity arguments, and a claimed privacy benefit from one-time remote inference. It acknowledges uncertain benchmark exposure for GPT/Llama and unequal settings in external comparisons. New Appendix E identifies class-balanced sampling, lack of guaranteed improvement over zero-shot prediction, and untested non-foundation-model noise as limitations.

D1.justification: v2 documents GPU hardware, distillation-stage training, additional image-model configurations, split sources, class-balanced label sampling, chat-model prompts and parsing fallbacks, and feature/embedding concatenation implementations. Appendix D.4 adds measured memory and training time. Audio, RoBERTa, and coarse-label implementation details disappear with their experiments; no new code release is identified.

R1.justification: A new knowledge-distillation subsection substantially redirects positioning toward student-teacher methods, adding discussion and citations including SelKD, multistage collaborative distillation, and DisCo. The earlier side-information and multitask-learning framing recedes. Appendix C develops comparisons with foundation-model prompt tuning, and the novelty argument becomes jointly using labels, unlabeled data, and teacher outputs.

P1.justification: The abstract, most of the introduction, motivation, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Baseline material is redistributed between Section 5 and Appendix C, implementation material is consolidated in Appendix B, and the appendices gain expanded motivation and limitations sections. The title drops 'Noisy,' and ZMT terminology is replaced by ZeroMatch.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn as a two-stage pipeline. Both training-accuracy figures and the feature-comparison matrix disappear. Benchmark tables are reorganized by teacher family, CLIP results move to the appendix, and new tables display zero-shot selection, external comparisons, ablations, embedding results, and computational costs.

improvement.justification: v2 improves assessability through component comparisons, measured runtime and memory, and specific limitations. It also removes v1's overstated 56% headline: the cited UrbanSound error change from 49.10 to 31.42 is approximately 36%. These gains are moderated by fewer established SSL comparators and reporting inconsistencies, including CIFAR100 CLIP-large zero-shot accuracy of 62.27% in v2 Table 7 versus 60.65% in Table 14.
